transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Liam O'Connor, Maya Chen, Dr. Priya Singh (Redwood) — Elena Morales, Samir Patel, Jenna Lee, Marcus Holt (GalaxyWare)

Auto Summary:
Quick implementation kickoff to align on runtime configuration, VPC/on-prem options, security posture, and an initial benchmarking plan. Focus on latency targets for customer-facing chat (~200ms p95) and cost constraints for high query volume. Next steps include staging access, sharing SOC2/network checklist, and a deep SE session on VPC peering and KMS.

Topics:
- Intro + roles
- High-level success criteria and timeline
- Network & security (VPC, peering, KMS)
- Deployment mode options: hosted vs dedicated vs private
- Initial benchmarking and sample data
- Observability and alerting requirements

Action items (recap included above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Liam O'Connor: hey everyone, thanks for squeezing this in, i'm Liam from Redwood — account exec on this one. quick round robin?
[00:10] Elena Morales: hi all, Elena here, CTO at GalaxyWare. excited to get started.
[00:14] Samir Patel: Samir, Platform eng, i'll own the infra side.
[00:17] Jenna Lee: Jenna, product — i'll own success metrics and acceptance criteria.
[00:21] Marcus Holt: Marcus, security lead. i'll, uh, drive compliance asks.
[00:25] Liam: sweet, thanks. on our side Maya's CSM, and priya is our SE — you'll hear priya get into the technical weeds.
[00:32] Maya Chen: hi all, looking forward to partnering on the onboarding runway.
[00:35] Dr. Priya Singh: hi, thanks. i'll try not to monopolize the mic but i will ask a lot of questions around traffic patterns.

[02:05] Liam: to set context — GalaxyWare wants to embed a realtime assistance feature in product with a target p95 latency around two hundred ms for short responses, supporting roughly 150k queries/day at peak. is that still the right framing?
[02:20] Jenna: yeah that's the target; we also need cost per 1k tokens to be inside our budget, so tradeoffs matter.
[02:28] Elena: timeline is Q1 pilot, production by mid Q2 pending the pilot results.

[04:10] Priya: quick clarifying question — is this mostly chat style short-turn convos, or long form generation? length distributions?
[04:18] Jenna: 80% short turns < 120 tokens, 20% longer summaries 600+ tokens.
[04:25] Priya: perfect — that shapes whether we push for aggressive batching, caching, or keep low-latency single-turn routing.

[06:00] Samir: we have a VPC in aws us-west-2, corporate firewall rules are strict. we prefer private deployment but open to dedicated if required.
[06:12] Marcus: for security we need audit logs, SSO via SAML, and key management using our Hashi vault — probably H-M or KMS. also we need data residency controls.
[06:25] Priya: got it. quick note — our Private offering supports customer-managed VPC peering and HSM/KMS integrations. Dedicated can be an intermediate where we hold capacity but enable VPC tunnel. there are nuance tradeoffs: private gives max isolation, dedicated faster to stand up.

[08:40] Liam: question for galaxyware — what's the preferred auth model for end-user requests? do you plan to proxy through your backend or expose tokens to clients?
[08:52] Elena: we proxy through backend. tokens never hit client.
[08:56] Maya: great, that simplifies token rotation and rate limiting on your end.

[10:30] Priya: on the runtime side, our serving runtime can do continuous batching and prefix kv caching. sometimes transcripts show it as K-V cash in auto trans — sorry, that's our speech-to-text — but it's KV cache. caching helps for repeated system prompts and shared context; but with low-latency targets, we may need to limit batch sizes on the chat path.

[12:50] Jenna: how do we balance batch size and p95 latency? can we see recommendations?
[12:58] Priya: yes — we'll run latency vs throughput sweep with your sample workload. expected trade: larger batch -> lower cost/throughput, higher tail latency. we'll recommend per-route configs: small batches + fast-path kernels for chat, larger batches for async re-ranks.

[15:20] Samir: network question — to peer with Redwood private control plane, do we need static routes? what's the firewall hole set?
[15:32] Priya: typically we ask for outbound TLS to a set of IPs and a CIDR for peering. our network checklist doc has specifics — we'll share it. probably port 443 outbound plus BGP for private peering if you choose that route.

[17:45] Marcus: encryption at rest — we need to ensure model caches or logs aren't stored unencrypted. do you support customer-managed KMS?
[17:56] Priya: yes, KMS integrations supported. we can also configure audit log forwarding to your SIEM. we'll note that in SOC2 docs.

[20:22] Liam: just to surface pricing/ops — if you go hosted vs dedicated vs private, cost and lead time change. Hosted fastest, lowest startup friction. Dedicated gives reserved capacity and more predictable p99 under burst, private gives full isolation but longer lead. what are your procurement constraints?
[20:45] Elena: legal prefers private but we might pilot on dedicated to move faster. procurement will want a clear SOW.

[23:10] Jenna: acceptance criteria — for pilot we want: p95 < 250ms for 90% of short-turns, throughput to sustain expected peak without errors, and automated alerts on errors and latency regressions.
[23:24] Maya: i'll capture that in the runbook.

[25:00] Priya: benchmarking plan proposal: you provide 5 canonical prompts + a 1% slice of your prod-ish dataset (anonymized). we will run three configs: hosted low-latency, dedicated medium batch, private with customer KMS to validate overhead. results include p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens.
[25:22] Samir: timeline for that?
[25:26] Priya: we can start within 48 hours of staging access; benchmark run takes 2 business days plus analysis.

[28:40] Liam: ok next, observability — what level of tracing do you need?
[28:48] Jenna: request/response trace, token-level cost, and per-route latency dashboards.
[28:55] Maya: Redwood Console exposes per-route dashboards and token breakdowns, and we can set retention windows depending on plan.

[31:10] Marcus: compliance question — do you provide a shared responsibility matrix so procurement can review?
[31:18] Maya: yes i'll share a matrix and our SOC2 package.

[33:05] Priya: about model variants — if you need deterministic shorter responses we can pin to quantized variants; otherwise for higher quality we use FP16 variants which may raise cost. sometimes our speech transbot writes FP16 as 'F-P-16', it's weird.

[35:40] Samir: what about rollout strategy — can we do canaries?
[35:46] Priya: absolutely — Console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback to a cheaper model if quality/regressions are detected. e.g., route 10% to new model, monitor eval prompts, if metrics drop revert.

[38:00] Jenna: about data retention — we need logs for debugging but must ensure retention limits and deletion hooks.
[38:10] Maya: we support configurable retention. we'll include deletion SLAs in the runbook.

[40:20] Liam: procurement note — we'll provide a sample SOW and optional reserved capacity options.
[40:28] Elena: good. procurement will want a ballpark number for a pilot.
[40:33] Liam: estimate: for a 3-week pilot with moderate traffic, hosted bench cost is low; dedicated pilot is a monthly reservation prorated — we'll follow up with numbers in a separate pricing email.

[43:12] Priya: technical deep-dive items we'll want if you pick private: IP ranges, peering model, cert exchange, and KMS access patterns. we can schedule a 90min SE deep dive.
[43:25] Samir: yes please, let's do that the week after next.

[45:00] Maya: recap of open items — i'll send runbook, SOC2 pack, staging invite, and Notion link.

[46:10] Marcus: a small nit — we use HashiCorp Vault and prefer HSM-backed keys. any quirk?
[46:20] Priya: we have a Vault integration pattern. we'll document the API calls for key wrap/unwrap.

[48:30] Elena: curious about fallback behavior — if primary model is down, is there automatic routing to another region/model?
[48:40] Priya: yes, smart routing supports region fallback and model variant fallback. if region is degraded we can route to a compatible quantized variant in another region with minor perf delta.

[51:05] Jenna: can you also run a few prompt-evals against our acceptance prompt set during benchmark?
[51:12] Priya: yes, include eval harness. we will attach quality regression metrics and highlight any hallucination incidents.

[53:40] Samir: how do we get the staging creds?
[53:44] Liam: i'll share an invite link and seed API key for staging. please rotate on your side.

[55:10] Maya: i'll drop links: runbook, network checklist, SOC2, staging invite, pricing sketch. also i'll create the Notion space.

[57:00] Marcus: timeline again — we expect procurement to review by 11/16. could you have the SOW and initial pricing by 11/06?
[57:12] Liam: yes, we'll try to get SOW + pricing by 11/06.

[59:45] Jenna: final check — acceptance criteria and sample prompts, we'll share later today.
[59:50] Elena: thanks everyone.
[59:55] Priya: thanks — Priya signing off but i'll follow up with the SE checklist.
[60:10] Maya: thanks all, we'll send notes and next steps.
[60:20] Liam: great talk to you all — meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, "H-M" for HSM) present. Links referenced: https://redwood.ai/staging-quickstart (placeholder), [SOC2 package link], [network-checklist link].

Recap (short):
- Pilot goals: p95 latency target ~200-250ms for short-turn chat, Q1 pilot, mid-Q2 GA if pilot successful.
- Security: need SOC2 docs, SAML SSO, Vault/KMS integration, audit log forwarding.
- Networking: GalaxyWare will share CIDR and firewall windows; Redwood to share peering checklist.
- Benchmarks: Redwood SE to run three configs once GalaxyWare provides sample prompts & data.
- Next meeting: SE deep-dive to cover VPC peering & KMS (proposed week of 2026-11-09).

End of transcript.
